title: Electron Paramagnetic Resonance on a Tip Reveals Thickness-Dependent Spin Heterogeneity in Two-
abstract: Direct characterization of the spin centers that provide the magnetic states of low-dimensional magnetic materials is key to understand whether the magnetic properties arise from defects, interfaces, or surface-specific coordination environments, and how they can thus be employed in devices. The spectroscopic technique par excellence for this purpose is electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) which has seen recent expansion to single spins but remains challenging for nanostructures on insulating surfaces.

title: From Retrosynthetic Prediction to the Bench: Experimental Evaluation of Computer-Generated Synthetic Routes
abstract: Retrosynthesis tools propose bond disconnections and precursor assignments, but the chemist must still evaluate these choices and select reaction conditions and purification before a route can be run. In this work, we examine 53 PostEra Manifold and AiZynthFinder proposals for three small organic targets by combining chemist assessments with selected synthesis outcomes. Proposals were rejected or deprioritised for different reasons: incorrect connectivity, unsupported transformations, or extra steps and costly precursors in routes that would otherwise work.

title: High-Throughput Compositional Tuning of Thin-Film (La,Ca)MnO 3 Perovskites as Bifunctional Oxygen Catalysts
abstract: Systematic investigations of composition-dependent performance in thin-film material libraries help to understand how descriptors influence performance and enable materials optimization. The fundamental challenges of such studies are the discrete synthesis of multiple compositions within one material family and the subsequent characterization steps, which are time-consuming and limit experimental throughput. In this work, the A-site-substituted thin-film (La,Ca)MnO 3 (LCMO) material family is studied for oxygen electrocatalysis performance.

title: Kinetically Synchronized Aqueous Co-precipitation and Hydrothermal Crystallisation of (Mg1−xCox)CO3 Rhombohedral Solid-Solution Nanoparticles: Thermodynamic Feasibility, Ethylene Glycol Kinetic Control, and Prospective Functional Applications
abstract: Cobaltoan magnesite, (Mg1−xCox)CO3 (R3c; x = 0–1), has previously been accessible only under extreme solid-state conditions (≥600 °C, ≥15 kbar; Goldsmith & Northrop, 1965) or over geological timescales in supergene ore environments (Barton et al., 2014). We report the first deliberate laboratory synthesis of phase-pure (Mg,Co)CO3 solid-solution nanoparticles at 250 °C under autogenous pressure (~40 bar) via a modified polyol-assisted aqueous coprecipitation route.

title: Redox-mediated water electrolysis for on-demand hydrogen production and low-grade heat harvesting
abstract: Hydrogen is widely regarded as a key energy carrier for a sustainable, decarbonized economy; however, conventional and decoupled water electrolysis remain highly electricity-intensive because of the thermodynamic water-splitting voltage and sluggish reaction kinetics. Here, we report a thermally regenerative electrochemical cycle (TREC)-based decoupled water electrolysis strategy that incorporates low-grade waste heat to enable hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) at cathodic potentials more positive than 0 V versus RHE (after IR correction).

title: Stepwise reduction of a porphyrin nanowire: minimal structural reorganization up to the open-shell tetraanion
abstract: π-Conjugated porphyrin oligomers serve as molecular wires: they exhibit high single-molecule conductance and excellent cycling kinetics as organic active electrode materials. These applications require systems in which charge/discharge cycles cause minimal changes in molecular geometry. Here, we use a butadiyne-linked porphyrin dimer as a model compound to show that its chemical reduction with alkali metals leads to subtle changes in the bond lengths in the resulting multiply charged anions, as revealed crystallographically.

title: Analysis of the pH-Dependent Phase Behavior of Amorphous Solid Dispersions Using in situ Stimulated Raman Scattering Microscopy
abstract: In this study, in situ stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) microscopy was employed as a novel analytical method to investigate the pH-dependent phase behavior of amorphous solid dispersions (ASDs) during hydration. Ibuprofen–poly(1-vinylpyrrolidone-co-vinyl acetate) (IBU-PVPVA) ASDS were used as model systems. The ASDs underwent multiple structural changes including polymer swelling, gel-layer formation and phase separation.

title: The Problem of NMR Data Analysis in Synthetic Chemistry: Why Is It Important to Understand Spectra?
abstract: High-resolution NMR (nuclear magnetic resonance) is one of the key methods for establishing the structures of organic compounds. Modern instrumentation and reference data provide a sufficient range of experiments for unambiguous assignment. However, in practice these resources are applied selectively. An assignment is commonly treated as complete once it no longer contradicts the expected structure. It is complete only when the spectrum as a whole has been explained, including signals at odds with that structure.

title: Engineering Fe-based OER electrocatalyst stability through alloy-driven modulation of Fe-O bond covalency and hydroxyl coverage
abstract: Fe-based oxyhydroxides are earth-abundant alternatives to costly Ir and Ru catalyst for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), but their stability in alkaline electrolyte limits their applicability at scale. We show that alloying FeOOH with 4+ ions (My = Se, Sn, Ti, Hf) controls dissolution through the electronegatiity of the alloyed element. In 1 M KOH at 10 mA cm-2, all four alloys exhibited slower steady-state (8–48 h) Fe dissolution rates relative to pure FeOOH; and corresponding first-order rate constants fit to transient mass loss data (enabled by XRF) decrease as My becomes less…

title: Cooling-induced liquid–liquid separation promotes monazite precipitation through segregation of rare earth elements
abstract: Monazite, (Ce,La,Nd)PO4, is a major source of rare earth elements (REEs), which play a vital role in green technology and electronics industries. Investigation into mechanisms of monazite formation from silicic melts provide valuable insights into its stability and behavior at varying temperature. This knowledge is crucial for improving the efficiency of REE extraction from mine slags, which could potentially contribute to expanding demand for critical materials.

title: First principles study of stability, electronic and optical properties of Diphenylhexatriene under pressure
Electronic and Steric Effects on the Photoswitching and Thermal Relaxation of Ortho-Substituted Pyrazole Azo Phthalimides
abstract: A series of ortho-substituted phthalimide–azopyrazole photoswitches bearing CH3, CF3, tert-Bu, and Ph groups was developed to determine how local steric and electronic perturbations control photochemical addressability and thermal Z→E relaxation. The substituents strongly altered the preferred irradiation wavelength while producing modest differences in the attainable Z-rich photostationary states. The CF3 derivative underwent E→Z photoisomerization at 530 nm, whereas the other derivatives were switched at 370 nm.

title: A New Route to Macrobicyclic Dibridgehead Diphopsphines P((CH 2 ) n ) 3 P; Reductive Demetalation of Cage-Like Fe(CO) 3 Adducts
abstract: When THF solutions of cage-like trans-Fe(CO) 3 (P((CH 2 ) n ) 3 P) ( 1 , n = a /10, b /12, c /14, d /16, e /18) are exposed to a potassium mirror, reduction occurs to give ferrate salts of the formula 2K + [(R 3 P)(CO) 3 Fe] 2– , as supported by IR data. Following additions of excess CO and methanol, the dibridgehead diphosphines P((CH 2 ) n ) 3 P ( 1a-e ) are isolated as white solids in 61-98% yields (average 80%) as mixtures of in/in and out/out isomers that interconvert by homeomorphic isomerization.

title: Lighten Learners’ Cognitive Load or Create Conceptual Understanding: Looking Beyond Le Chatelier’s Principle.
abstract: Here we explore a novel approach to teaching the effect of temperature on exothermic and endothermic reactions. We contend that Le Chatelier’s Principle is best used as a predictive tool. Insights from teacher practice, personal experience and action research are shared. This narrative is a reflective professional journey supported by empirical evidence from action research (n = 17). The insights gained offer strategies to build conceptual understanding by applying Johnstone’s Triangle to reactions like the Haber process.

title: Structural and Electrochemical Evaluations of Li4Ti5O12 Composite Anodes with an Organic Ionic Plastic Crystal Solid Electrolyte
abstract: Li 4 Ti 5 O 12 (LTO) is a commercialized anode active material for battery applications. Using LTO in solid-state batteries (SSBs) is expected to overcome some issues associated with anode active materials working at a low electrode potential, such as graphite and Si. Li+-containing organic ionic plastic crystals (OIPCs) reportedly have issues with these materials, including low Coulombic efficiency and achievable capacity relative to the theoretical value. This study explored the LTO−OIPC composite anode and evaluated its surface structure and electrochemical performance.

title: Base-Dependent Lewis Acidity in Substituted Boranes: Revisiting Intrinsic Acidity through DFT and Machine Learning
abstract: The Lewis acidity of boranes is strongly influenced by the electronic nature of their substituents and is commonly assessed through interactions with representative Lewis bases. However, the extent to which the relative Lewis acidity ordering of substituted boranes depends on the identity of the interacting Lewis base has not been systematically investigated. In this work, Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations combined with machine learning (ML) analysis were employed to quantify substituent effects and base dependence in borane–Lewis base interactions.

title: Beyond the Ligand Applicability Domain: Generalization and Local Resolution in Structure-Aware Foundation Models for Affinity Prediction
abstract: Structure-aware foundation models that jointly represent proteins and ligands promise to extend affinity prediction beyond the chemical applicability domains of conventional ligand-based models, but whether they provide sufficient resolution to guide fine-grained medicinal-chemistry decisions remains unclear. We evaluatedBoltz-2across12kinasetargetsusinghistoricalbioactivityreconstruction,binding-pocket randomization, cross-target selectivity analysis, and chemical-series evaluation.

title: Few-Shot Early-Release Adaptation Enables Generalizable Prediction of PLGA Drug Release
abstract: Reliable prediction of long-term drug release remains challenging for formulations developed under experimental conditions that differ from those represented in literature-derived training data. Standard formulation descriptors capture important physicochemical and formulation characteristics, but they do not fully represent study-specific factors that shape the realized release trajectory.

title: AI Agents for CRISPR Diagnostics: From Automation to Bounded Autonomy
abstract: Recent years have witnessed rapid advances in clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) diagnostics, artificial intelligence (AI), and self-driving laboratories for automation. CRISPR diagnostics have emerged as a promising strategy for earlier disease detection, with Cas12a and Cas13a targeting DNA and RNA, respectively, and converting that recognition into collateral reporter cleavage.

title: Synthesis of nitride materials by atmospheric pressure metathesis
abstract: Nitride materials have many important technological applications, yet they remain underexplored compared to other classes of compounds, as reflected by the smaller number of reports in databases and literature. The primary reason for this is the difficulty of synthesizing nitrides, which must outcompete energetically stable molecular N 2 and oxide compounds. As a result, bulk synthesis of nitrides often requires high pressure or corrosive fluxes in addition to oxygen-free conditions.

title: Surface-Aware Generative Design of Selective Inhibitors for Protein–Membrane Adsorption
abstract: Peripheral membrane proteins (PMPs) bind membrane surfaces through interfacial binding sites (IBSs) that are critical for stable membrane association and proper orientation of catalytic active sites. Dysregulated PMP–membrane interactions can enhance catalytic activity and contribute to diseases including cancer, but many PMPs remain difficult therapeutic targets because their active sites lack well-defined pockets or become accessible only upon membrane binding.

title: Improved electrostatic machine learning embedding ML/MM scheme for a phosphoryl transfer reaction
abstract: The promise of hybrid machine learning/molecular mechanics (ML/MM) simulations is to provide QM/MM-quality free energy profiles at a fraction of the cost. One of the challenges is to accurately treat the interaction between the ML subsystem and the MM environment. Here we test the Electrostatic ML Embedding (EMLE) scheme on a minimal model of RNA cleavage in water, which is already challenging due to a doubly charged reactant dissociating into two anions.

title: Two-Electron Photoreduction of Pd(II) Oxalates: In Crystallo Synthesis and Catalysis
abstract: Discovery and optimization of cross-coupling catalysts require catalyst activation strategies that balance the operational simplicity of air-stable precatalysts with the need for air-sensitive, lowcoordinate and -valent intermediates for substrate activation and turnover. Here we introduce a general approach for on-demand catalyst activation via two-electron photoreduction of air-stable phosphine-ligated palladium(II) oxalates. The platform exploits rapid ligand exchange at (MeCN)2Pd(ox) to enable modular assembly of catalyst photoprecursors from a single precursor.

title: Data-Driven Prospective Design of Phase-Inversion Conductive Polymer Membranes
abstract: Conductive polymer membranes combine separation and electrical functionality, but their design remains challenging because performance emerges from coupled effects of composition, fabrication, and operating conditions. Here, we assembled 396 membrane records from 77 publications and developed target-specific machine-learning models for pure-water permeability (PWP), solute rejection, and electrical conductivity.

title: Transition from Anisotropic to Isotropic Crystal Growth Enables Ultrahigh-Rate Zn Metal Anodes in Batteries
abstract: Achieving controllable crystallization under dynamic, far-from-equilibrium conditions remains a fundamental challenge underlying many technologically important processes, including highpower batteries based on metal anodes. Recent studies have identified crystal anisotropy as a key factor governing electrodeposit morphology. Departing from conventional wisdom, we find that suppressing highly anisotropic facet-dependent growth by slowing interfacial kinetics results in more isotropic, morphologically uniform electrodeposition.

title: Active-Space Selection in Nonadiabatic Dynamics Simulations of Dense Manifolds of Excited States: When Local Diabatization Needs Great Care
abstract: Local diabatization (LD) propagates electronic amplitudes using time-overlaps of adiabatic states and is robust to wavefunction phase arbitrariness, root character transport, and rotations within near-degenerate manifolds. However, when truncated dynamical bases are not numerically supported by the consecutive-geometry overlaps, polar orthogonalization underlying the LD approach can enforce unitary evolution in unresolved directions leading to unphysical population transfer. This work introduces an active-space screening protocol based on singular values of time-overlap matrices.

title: Understanding the Dynamics of C-OH Bond Activation over Mo 2 C under Hydrodeoxygenation Reaction Conditions
abstract: Hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) of biomass to value-added chemicals using transition metal carbides (TMCs) serves as a two-fold solution to overreliance on fossil-based feedstocks and excessive usage of noble metal catalysts. Specifically, Mo 2 C and W 2 C have emerged as viable alternatives to noble metal catalysts for HDO reactions. However, the underlying reaction mechanisms and structure-activity relationships for TMC catalysts are still not fully understood. Our previous mechanistic studies (Meena et al.

title: Enhancing double-duplex invasion by using multiple parallel-stranded peptide nucleic acids
abstract: Peptide nucleic acids (PNAs) enable sequence-specific recognition of double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) via invasion complex formation. Here, we report a strategy using multiple parallel-stranded PNAs to enhance invasion efficiency. Cooperative binding of PNAs at adjacent target sites markedly improved invasion efficiency and enabled sequence-specific recognition of plasmid DNA under physiological conditions.

title: Integrated Process Environmental and Economic Modeling of Electrically Assisted Forward Osmosis Microbial Desalination for Water and Struvite Recovery
abstract: Electrically assisted forward osmosis (eFO) coupled with a microbial desalination cell (MDC) integrates water recovery, nutrient recovery, desalination, and bioelectricity utilization. This study coupled a previously validated hybrid mechanistic–data-driven model with cradle-to-grave life cycle assessment (LCA) and techno-economic analysis (TEA) to evaluate the sustainability of eFO–MDC across operating conditions and scale-up scenarios.

title: Case Studies of Homemorphic Isomerization: Interconversion of In/Out Isomers of Bicyclo[6.5.1]tetradecane and Related Bicyclic Hydrocarbons
abstract: Homeomorphic isomerization is equivalent to turning a molecule inside out in the same manner as a reversible article of clothing. Manifestations include the interconversion of (a) in,in and out,out isomers, or (b) in,out and out,in isomers of bicyclic molecules, but without inverting the configurations of the bridgehead atoms. In this preprint, this topological process is probed computationally for the title molecules.

title: Homogeneous Electrochemical Hydrogenation of 1-Octene with [( iPr PNP)CoCl] and Water
abstract: Here we present the electrochemical hydrogenation (ECH) of 1-octene to n -octane using the homogeneous complex [( iPr PNP)CoCl] [CoCl] and water as the source of hydrogen atoms. We showcase how tuning only electrode surface area, as well as supporting electrolyte type and concentration can drastically increase the reaction selectivity for ECH over parasitic H 2 evolution from initially 9% to eventually 82% faradaic efficiency, without traditional chemical reaction optimization or catalyst tuning.

title: Inconsistent odor-threshold measurements limit prediction from molecular structure
abstract: Existing work treats odor detection threshold prediction as a supervised regression problem, assuming published thresholds are clean targets. In current public datasets, they are not: values come from different measurement sources and often disagree for the same molecule. Across the three largest public air-phase compilations, thresholds for identical molecules differ systematically by median factors of 3 to 11.

title: Atomic Level Characterization of PolyGlycine Assembly
abstract: Polyglycine peptides can adopt polyproline II (PPII) helical conformations that assemble into honeycomb-shaped oligomers. These polyglycine II (PGII) helical bundles, which are also found in several natural proteins, lack apolar groups and cannot be stabilized by hydrophobic interactions. Thus, their folding must differ from that of typical globular proteins for which hydrophobic interactions promote structure formation. Despite their fundamental interest and relevance for molecular pathology, the atomic level details on how these PGII assemblies form are scarcely explored.

title: Mechanism-grounded fragmentation trees enable explicit chemical reasoning for electron ionization mass spectrum prediction
abstract: Developing predictive models that connect molecular structures with measured spectra while preserving interpretable links to ion formation and fragmentation chemistry remains a central challenge in predictive spectroscopy. Here we present FragTreeMS, a mechanism-grounded framework that decomposes electron ionization (EI) mass spectrum prediction into fragmentation tree generation and repair followed by pathway- conditioned intensity learning.

title: Exploring intermediates in mechanochemical cycle and mechanism of regulation of full-length Dynein
abstract: Cytoplasmic dynein is a complex hexameric AAA+ motor protein essential for intracellular transport, yet the structural mechanisms and domain cooperativity driving its mechanochemical cycle remain incompletely understood. In this study, we utilize a dual-basin structure-based model (SBM) to simulate the full-length dynein cycle in the presence of microtubules. Rather than a single concerted transition, our results reveal that dynein moves through discrete, on-pathway conformational intermediates, including a transient, ADP-bound state that bridges the pre- and post-powerstroke configurations.

title: Water-Responsive Shape-Memory Origami Enabled by a Washi–Bulk pNIPAAm Hydrogel Hybrid Sheet
abstract: Origami transforms two-dimensional sheets into complex three-dimensional forms through folding and has evolved from a traditional art into a versatile design principle for deployable and reconfigurable structures. Here, we develop a water-responsive shape-memory origami sheet by combining highly concentrated poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (bulk pNIPAAm) hydrogel with Japanese kozo paper.

title: Self-quenched growth of monodisperse SnO2 nanocrystals—insensitive to synthesis conditions
abstract: Metal oxide thin film fabrication from colloidal nanocrystal dispersions separates the materials synthesis from the device (layer) fabrication, enabling fast solution processing. However, nanocrystal ink syntheses can be still too complex to be truly scalable for large-area ultra-lowcost applications such as solar modules. Here, we present a self-quenched (by precipitation) nanocrystal synthesis at room temperature. The synthesis is independent of the precursor concentrations, precursor addition speed (injection vs.

title: Beyond Organic Molecules: MetalLipoDB, a Lipophilicity Dataset for Metal Complexes and Machine Learning Benchmarks
abstract: Lipophilicity governs the uptake, distribution and toxicity of drug candidates, yet the experimental logP datasets used to build predictive models contain almost exclusively organic molecules. Here we present MetalLipoDB, a manually curated dataset of 5158 experimental logP and logD values of complexes of 23 metals from 1192 articles, including 556 entries for multinuclear and heterometallic complexes, annotated with the measurement conditions and counterions.

title: Machine Learning-Guided QSAR Modeling and Virtual Screening of Medicinal Plant-Derived Phytochemicals for the Identification of Potential hDHFR Inhibitors
abstract: Human dihydrofolate reductase (hDHFR) is a well-established anticancer drug target due to its essential role in folate metabolism and DNA synthesis. This study employed integrated machine based structural-activity relationship, virtual screening, and molecular docking to identify potential hDHFR inhibitors from medicinal plant-derived phytochemicals. A curated dataset of 1,368 compounds was obtained from ChEMBL and presented using Morgan fingerprints and RDKit molecular descriptors. Four regression model algorithms, including RF, XGBoost, LightGBM, and SVR were developed and optimized.

title: On the Mechanism of Catalytic Chain Transfer Photopolymerization (CCTP2): the Good, the Bad and the Ugly
abstract: Previously, the addition of catalytic quantities of cobalt(II) complexes to standard methacrylatebased formulations was found to reduce the crosslinking density, glass transition temperature, modulus and stiffness of the resultant photopolymeric materials proportional to catalyst loading. We have dubbed this technique catalytic chain transfer photopolymerization (CCTP2), which is conceptually and mechanistically linked to its predecessor catalytic chain transfer polymerization (CCTP), but uses photoinitiation, multifunctional methacrylate monomers, and creates crosslinked 2 materials.

title: Electrochemical Detection of Ethanol in Liquid Samples and Simulated Breath: Investigating Calibration, Selectivity, and Preconcentration
abstract: Advances in miniaturized and point-of-care electrochemical sensors have expanded their applications in healthcare, environmental monitoring, and public safety. Consequently, it is important to study the principles of these technologies in an undergraduate setting. This experiment uses screen-printed electrodes for electrochemical detection of ethanol and introduces students to electrocatalysis, calibration curves, chemical interference, selectivity, and preconcentration.

title: Practical In Situ Generation of Phosphorus Pentafluoride as a Metal-Free Potent Lewis Acid
abstract: Metal-free potent Lewis acids are of great interest in the pharmaceutical and food industries to avoid metal contaminants. Phosphorus pentafluoride (PF 5 ) is a potent Lewis acid, but its practical use is severely restricted by its gaseous state and corrosiveness. Here we report a simple and convenient method for either the rapid or slow in situ generation of PF 5 from widely available and easy to handle hexafluorophosphate (PF 6 − ) salts and either aluminum chloride (AlCl 3 ) or boron trifluoride etherate (BF 3 ·Et 2 O), respectively.

title: Parallel Production of Uniform Artificial Multicellular Models Using Vibration-Induced Local Microvortices
abstract: In this study, we propose a facile and efficient method for constructing artificial multicellular models via vibration-induced flow (VIF), a local fluid flow induced around vibrating microstructures. By applying circular vibration to a substrate with a cylindrical micropillar array, uniform micro-vortices were generated, into which giant unilamellar vesicles (GUVs), as artificial cells, rapidly accumulated at the center. We show that by modifying two GUV populations with complementary single-stranded DNAs, we can promote specific adhesion between GUVs, leading to uniform parallel aggregates.

title: A Highly Proton-Tolerant Multicenter Borane/Phosphazene Catalytic System for Efficient PO/CO2 Copolymerization toward CO2-Based Poly(carbonate-ether) Polyols
abstract: Low-molecular-weight CO2-based poly(carbonate-ether) polyols from ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP) of propylene oxide (PO) with CO2 are highly desired as soft blocks to synthesize sustainable polyurethanes. However, such process remains great challenges because of the demanding of highly proton-tolerant catalysts. Herein, we report a binary organocatalysis system based on a nanoscopic multicenter borane Lewis acid (POSS-B8) combined with various organobases for the tunable ROCOP of PO and CO2.

title: Growth-Triggered Nano-vesicle Budding via Leaflet Area Asymmetry in Fatty-Acid Protocells
abstract: Fatty-acid vesicles growing by monomer uptake, as demonstrated experimentally for Szostak-type protocells, insert new amphiphiles predominantly into the outer leaflet. Because transbilayer flip-flop is not instantaneous, this generates a growing area mismatch between the two leaflets. We show, using the area-difference-elasticity (ADE) framework for vesicle shape, that this mismatch crosses a threshold beyond which the vesicle relieves it by shedding small, high-curvature nano-vesicles rather than by symmetric division–with no external mechanical forcing required.

title: Atomically Precise Platinum Nanocluster Catalysts for Efficient Hydrogen Production via Methylcyclohexane Dehydrogenation
abstract: In hydrogen storage technologies with liquid organic hydrogen carriers, the development of efficient catalysts for methylcyclohexane dehydrogenation is highly important. In this study, we developed atomically precise platinum nanocluster catalysts supported on Al2O3 (Ptx/Al2O3; x = 17, ~51). Comprehensive characterization demonstrated that the catalysts remained highly monodisperse and of uniform particle size (0.86 or 1.15 nm), and maintained a cationic electronic state (Ptδ+) even after thermal treatment.

title: Experimental Inter-Report Scatter Bounds Machine-Learning Accuracy for TADF Singlet–Triplet Gaps—Structure and Semi-Empirical Features Reach the Same Limit
abstract: The singlet–triplet gap ∆ESTis the screening parameter for thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF), yet independent experimental reports of the same compound scatter by 0.072 eV RMS, and the per-molecule median regressed on is known only to 0.049 eV, about half of any model’s error. This label noise sets a ceiling on every predictor, yet the models sit below it: neither noise nor capacity alone accounts for the remaining error.

title: Continuous-wave laser ablation enables high-resolution ambient mass spectrometry imaging
abstract: Continuous-wave lasers are generally not considered for applications demanding precision ablation, because sustained heating in bulk tissue causes extensive thermal damage. Here we show that this limitation does not apply to thin sections: a 2.91 µm continuous-wave laser leaves no resolvable heat-affected zone beyond the ablation track on 10 µm thick cryosections, a confinement consistent with heat sinking vertically into the glass slide rather than diffusing laterally.

title: Ligand Engineering of an N-Heterocyclic Carbene Au13 Nanocluster as a Strong Photoreductant for Sensitized Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction
abstract: Developing photosensitizers with enhanced photoredox potential while preserving superior visible-light absorption and sufficient excited-state lifetimes poses a formidable challenge in photocatalytic redox reactions. In this study, we synthesized a series of bis-N-heterocyclic carbene Au13 nanoclusters (bis-NHC Au13 NCs) functionalized with various electron-donating/withdrawing groups.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Towards Zero-Waste PFAS Treatment Train: Regeneration of Ion Exchange Resins in Supercritical CO 2 Coupled with Supercritical Water Oxidation
abstract: Ion-exchange resins (IXRs) are often used to remove PFAS from aqueous matrices; however, spent media generate secondary waste that must be disposed of. We demonstrate a waste-treatment strategy that combines IXR regeneration in a supercritical carbon dioxide (scCO 2 ) environment followed by destruction of PFAS-containing regenerants via supercritical water oxidation (SCWO). Screening of co-solvent formulation showed that HCl-amended ethanol/water mixture effectively extracted PFOA from both macroporous and gel-type resins marketed for single use.

title: The impacts of polystyrene nanoplastics on colorectal cancer: Evidence from integrated network toxicity and in vitro approaches
abstract: Environmental ingestion of polystyrene nanoplastics (PNPLs) raises critical public health concerns, yet their impacts on colorectal cancer (CRC) remain obscure. In this study, network toxicology, and in vitro validation were integrated to evaluate the molecular mechanisms linking PNPLs to CRC. We identified 154 overlapping targets by integrating GEO-derived differentially expressed genes with PNPLs-predicted targets and CRC-associated genes, which are enriched in pathways associated with cancer signaling, apoptosis, oxidative stress, and inflammation.

title: Plasmon-Driven Urea Photosynthesis on a Rationally Designed RuCu Nanoalloy Cocatalyst Through a Kinetically Favorable C–N Coupling Mechanism
abstract: Photocatalytic urea synthesis from N2 and CO2 offers a sustainable alternative to the energy-intensive industrial process. However, the efficiency remains hindered by the sluggish C–N coupling kinetics. Herein, a new, kinetically favorable urea synthesis pathway is achieved by a rationally designed RuCu alloy/plasmonic WO3–x hybrid photocatalyst. A remarkable urea production rate of 750 μg gcat–1 h–1 together with a solar-to-chemical conversion efficiency of 0.072% is obtained under simulated sunlight illumination, outperforming those of most reported systems.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Copper-Catalyzed Ring-Opening Hydroboration and Enantioselective Cascade Hydroboration/Protoboration of Arylidenecyclobutanes
abstract: Arylidenecyclobutanes (ACBs) are an emerging class of five-carbon synthons for the construction of structurally complex molecules. Organoboron compounds are of central importance in modern synthetic chemistry; herein, we report copper-catalyzed ring-opening hydroboration and enantioselective cascade hydroboration/protoboration reactions that use arylidenecyclobutanes as C5 building blocks to access linear (E)–1,4-alkenylboronates and chiral 1,4-diboronates, respectively.

title: Orthogonal nucleophile-ordered assembly for modular access to enantiopure 1,2-amino alcohols
Physicists just found the ‘ghost’ of superconductivity
abstract: Physicists have found striking evidence for an unusual form of superconducting behavior in uranium ditelluride, where electron pairs organize into rippling patterns called pair density waves. Even more surprisingly, these patterns appear to survive after ordinary superconductivity disappears, suggesting that the electron pairs responsible for superconductivity may begin forming before the material actually becomes superconducting.

title: Spatially Refined Analysis of Emission Burdens and Equity from Light-, Medium-, and Heavy-Duty Vehicle Traffic in the United States
abstract: We estimate block-level emission intensities of nitrogen oxides (NO X ) and fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) from on-road vehicle traffic for every census block in the United States, combining MOVES-based emission factors with street level traffic data. We use this spatially refined, computationally efficient, and policy-sensitive metric to evaluate emissions burden.

title: Effect of Zinc Incorporation on the Structure, Conductivity and (Electro)chemical Stability of Li6–2 x Zn x PS5X (X = Br, Cl, I) Argyrodite Solid Electrolytes
abstract: Solid-state batteries (SSBs) are currently regarded as a potential alternative to dominant liquid-electrolyte Li-ion batteries, possibly offering higher energy and power densities. In this regard, lithium argyrodite solid electrolytes have received considerable attention due to their high ionic conductivity and mechanical softness allowing straightforward integration into SSB cells. However, they face issues with (electro)chemical stability leading to an accelerated capacity fade. Thus, mitigation strategies have been pursued via chemical substitution.

title: The scaffold nucleoporin Nup188 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation
abstract: Components of nuclear pore complexes are broadly classified into two categories: intrinsically disordered FG-repeat nucleoporins such as Nup98, which can undergo liquid-liquid phase separation, and scaffold nucleoporins, which form the NPC's structural framework. The basis for crosstalk of these nucleoporins within NPC and beyond is poorly understood. Here we show that human Nup188, a helical inner-ring scaffold protein, forms condensates both in purified form as well as at endogenous level.

title: The biophysical interaction network that couples zona occludens-1 to membrane proteins at tight junctions
abstract: Tight junctions are dynamic membrane-bound protein assemblies that maintain barrier function for tissues as cells divide, grow, and move through development and throughout life. Maintenance of tissue barriers requires spatially separated intracellular and extracellular signaling pathways to be linked through novel and dynamic protein interaction networks. Tight junction intracellular signaling is governed by zona occludens-1 (ZO-1), a Membrane-Associated GUanylate Kinase (MAGUK) family protein that recruits and assembles transmembrane proteins and scaffolds them to the actin cytoskeleton…

title: Structure-based virtual screening reveals new metabolite interactions and modulators of human glucose-6-phosphate isomerase
abstract: Exploring the ability of metabolic enzymes to interact with diverse small molecules can provide insights into their ligand recognition and activity regulation. Glucose-6-phosphate isomerase (GPI) is an enzyme that catalyzes the second step of glycolysis, a critical node that links glucose metabolism to other cytosolic pathways, such as pentose phosphate and hexosamine biosynthetic pathways. Despite its importance in cellular metabolism, little is known about the broad ligandability of GPI. Here, we performed a structure-based virtual screening using molecular docking to identify new modulators predicted to engage with the human GPI active site. Enzyme kinetic and binding studies confirmed eleven compounds as active-site binders of GPI, exhibiting inhibitory activities and binding affinities in upper micromolar to sub-millimolar range. The binding of several ligands to GPI active site was further supported by X-ray crystallographic data. In addition, in vitro assays were performed to evaluate the modulatory effects of the GPI hits on cellular glycolysis and viability. The identified inhibitors included the mono-phosphorylated metabolite of ribavirin, which inhibited glycolytic flux and cell viability; two compounds with phosphate bioisosteres; and endogenous phosphate-containing metabolites from the pentose phosphate, hexosamine, nucleotide, and mevalonate pathways. Collectively, these findings expanded the repertoire of human GPI ligands and revealed previously unrecognized GPI-metabolite interactions that may contribute to modulation of glycolytic flux.

title: Releasing Protein Cargo from Synthetic Cells by Coupling Cell-Free Expression to Osmotic Actuation
abstract: Macromolecular release from synthetic cells often relies on membrane pores or channels. We explored whether internally generated osmotic stress could increase membrane permeability and promote release. Using double-emulsion microfluidics, we encapsulated an Escherichia coli cell-free expression system in Pluronic L121 polymersomes to co-express the fluorescent protein mScarlet3 and the dextranase PsDex1711 in the presence of dextran. PsDex1711-mediated dextran hydrolysis produced a greater increase in bulk osmolality than reactions without PsDex1711 DNA. Tracking hundreds of individual polymersomes showed that PsDex1711-containing populations expanded, whereas control populations contracted. The distribution of normalized fluorescence revealed a subset with lower residual fluorescence than the main population. In selected expanded polymersomes, integrated internal mScarlet3 fluorescence declined to 18-22% of peak levels, without visible membrane disruption, consistent with protein release. These findings support a proof of concept for using internal gene expression to promote macromolecular release through osmotic actuation without introducing dedicated membrane pores.

title: Activation pathway of the human voltage-gated proton channel
abstract: Many protein functions are coupled to proton transfer, yet the underlying mechanisms remain extremely difficult to resolve by experiment or conventional molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The human voltage-gated proton channel HV1 (hHV1) plays key roles in human physiology, but how voltage and pH together drive its activation remains unresolved. Experimental structures of hHV1 are limited to the X-ray structure of a mouse chimera and NMR models of a truncated hHV1, both representing an intermediate resting state. Here we determine the activation pathway of hHV1, together with structural models of its resting and activated states, using an approach that integrates all-atom continuous constant-pH MD (CpHMD), weighted-ensemble (WE) path sampling, and AlphaFold modeling. Starting from an AlphaFold model selected for consistency with resting-state experimental data, over 100 s of simulations reveal a mechanism in which transmembrane voltage, assisted by proton titration, drives an outward displacement of the transmembrane segment S4 accompanied by a one-click reorganization of countercharge pairings. These events are enabled by a delicately balanced electrostatic landscape and pH-modulated breathing motions in the resting state that prime the channel for protonation-state switches upon voltage sensing, a principle that may underlie other proton-coupled voltage-gating processes. The simulations also uncover lipid-binding sites at which POPG selectively stabilizes the S4-up conformation, whereas POPE can stabilize either state. These predictions are validated against extensive electrophysiology, mutagenesis data, and new smFRET experiments, which support the one-click S4 displacement and the lipid effects. WE-CpHMD, implemented in the AMBER package, is applicable to other proton-coupled processes that remain elusive.

title: Aziridination-Based Crosslinking Enables Site-Resolved Elucidation of Lipid Binding and Protein Conformational Changes
abstract: Lipid–protein interactions play critical roles in cellular function, yet their site-resolved characterization remains challenging due to the dynamic nature of lipid binding and the limited availability of chemoselective strategies for covalently capturing native lipid–protein contacts. Here, we introduce aziridination-based lipid–protein crosslinking coupled with mass spectrometry (Azi-LPXL-MS), a chemoselective strategy that installs an N–H aziridine moiety onto acyl chains of native unsaturated lipids and enables subsequent crosslinking to proximal lysine residues using the amine-reactive reagent disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS). This integrated workflow simultaneously identifies lipid-binding sites and intraprotein peptide–peptide distance constraints, providing direct insight into lipid binding and binding-induced conformational changes within a single experiment. Application of Azi-LPXL-MS to β-lactoglobulin (BLG) demonstrates these capabilities, consistent with known structural models, while additionally providing solution-phase and conformational information not accessible from static structures alone. The power of the method is further demonstrated in the integral membrane enzyme diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1 (DGAT1). Azi-LPXL-MS reveals phosphatidic acid (PA)-binding sites and maps lipid-dependent conformational rearrangements across both resolved and previously uncharacterized regions. These data further define an allosteric conformational network linking lipid engagement to distal structural changes. Integrated with site-directed mutagenesis and molecular docking, two potential PA-binding sites in DGAT1, located in a surface pocket and an internal chamber, were identified and functionally validated, further supporting the experimental findings. These results establish Azi-LPXL-MS as a site-resolved method for studying lipid–protein interactions, providing insight into how individual lipid species engage proteins and influence their conformations in biological systems.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: What Random Splits Measure in Polymer Glass-Transition Prediction: Chemistry Holdouts, Applicability Domains, and Prior Integration
abstract: Predicting the glass-transition temperature (Tg) helps select polymers for a service-temperature window, but accuracy on familiar structures may not transfer to a new family. We compare validation protocols on 7367 curated homopolymers. Histogram gradient boosting gives R2 = 0.899 and mean absolute error (MAE) = 23.9 K under random cross-validation, 0.857 and 28.5 K under scaffold holdout, a class-macro mean of 0.355 and 43.3 K under curator-class holdout, and -3.79 and 79.5 K under high-Tg extrapolation.

title: Multiscale Molecular Orientation in Polyacrylonitrile Precursors for Carbon Fibers: Processing Regulation, Characterization Methodologies, and Structure-Property Correlations
abstract: Polyacrylonitrile (PAN) precursor fibers represent the dominant feedstock for manufacturing high-performance carbon fibers, and the hierarchical molecular orientation established during precursor processing fundamentally determines the tensile strength and elastic modulus of the final products. However, the precise regulation of multiscale orientational structures across spinning, hot-drawing, and thermal treatment stages remains a long-standing bottleneck for breaking the performance ceiling of carbon fibers.

title: Time-resolved monitoring of key tea fermentation indicators via Raman-NIR spectroscopic fusion and deep learning-based predictive modeling
abstract: Routine monitoring of black tea fermentation relies on destructive and time-consuming wet chemistry methods. Therefore, a non-destructive analytical strategy combining Raman and near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy with deep learning was developed for simultaneously monitoring key fermentation indicators. Fresh Camellia sinensis leaves were fermented for 4 h under controlled temperature and humidity, with samples collected at nine time points.

title: Resolving the Adsorption Geometries of Methanol on Anatase Titania (101) via Facet-Controlled Nanocrystals
abstract: Bridging the gap between single-crystal studies and technical catalysts is critical for understanding structure–function relationships in oxide catalysis. Here, we utilize hydroxyl- and partially water-covered anatase TiO2 nanocrystals with an exposure of the (101) facet exceeding 90% to resolve long-standing controversies in methanol adsorption geometry. We combine in situ DRIFTS conducted at atmospheric pressure with first-principles calculations to pinpoint species-specific vibrational signatures and reveal adsorbate geometries that are inaccessible to experiments alone.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Cation Vacancies with and without O–O Dimerization: Identifying Reconstructed Defect Configurations in Metal Oxides
abstract: Point defects in solid-state materials are conventionally modeled as lattice-derived defects, generated by adding or removing atoms from symmetric bulk lattice structures, followed by local geometry optimization. This approach often yields symmetric, weakly relaxed local minima that remain close to the parent lattice. Here, we show that this assumption can fail qualitatively for vacancies in many metal oxides. Rather than retaining a lattice-derived geometry with localized holes on oxygen sites, cation vacancies can drive extensive reconstruction, producing defect configurations in which the O–O bonds and O–O–O chains become the preferred charge-compensation motifs. We combined the minima hopping (MH) structure prediction algorithm with machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), hybrid QM/MM embedded-cluster calculations, and periodic density functional theory (DFT) calculations to investigate cation vacancies across a broad series of metal oxides. Our results show a clear oxidation-state-dependent trend. In the charge-neutral state, cation vacancies in oxides with formal oxidation states of +4 or higher favor reconstructed defect configurations containing O–O bonds or O–O–O chains with bond lengths of approximately 1.4 Å, lowering the defect formation energy by up to several electronvolts relative to the conventional structure. By contrast, in oxides with lower cation oxidation states, such reconstructions are generally unfavorable at charge neutrality but can become energetically more favorable at positive charge states. These findings define oxygen-bond formation as a general reconstruction pathway for cation vacancies in metal oxides and show that global structure searches are essential for predictive defect modeling beyond conventional lattice-derived local minima.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Structural basis of coiled-coil domain-mediated inhibition of A. baumannii AbTir NAD+ nucleosidase activity
abstract: TIR (Toll/interleukin-1 receptor) domains are central components of innate immunity and cell-death pathways across diverse forms of life. In bacteria, TIR domain-containing proteins participate in diverse antiphage defence systems, several of which rely on NADase activity carried out by TIR domains. This nucleosidase activity is often regulated by additional domains that modulate activation and specificity in response to infection. AbTir, a TIR domain-containing protein from Acinetobacter baumannii, contains an N-terminal CC domain that negatively regulates its NADase activity, but the structural basis of this regulation remains unknown. Here, we used X-ray crystallography to investigate the molecular basis of CC domain-mediated regulation in AbTir. We determined the crystal structure of full-length AbTir in complex with a nanobody, revealing a symmetric AbTir TIR dimer in which only one of the two symmetry-related CC helices is accommodated at the dimer surface, breaking the overall symmetry of the full-length protein. Structural comparisons with other bacterial TIR domains suggest that such TIR dimers likely represent an inactive state, in which the NAD+-binding site has not yet formed. Phylogenetic analysis places AbTir within a family of bacterial TIR proteins associated with defence-related genomic loci, although phage-spot assays performed in the surrogate host Escherichia coli did not detect measurable antiphage activity. Together, these findings reveal an unusual structural mechanism of CC domain-mediated inhibition of a bacterial TIR NADase and expand our understanding of the mechanistic diversity of bacterial TIR proteins.

title: Functional characterization of terpene synthases from Dendrobium nobile provides insights into the biosynthesis of copaborneol, a proposed dendrobine precursor
abstract: Picrotoxane-type sesquiterpene alkaloids, including dendrobine, are characteristic constituents of Dendrobium nobile, but the enzymes that produce their proposed skeletal precursors remain in completely characterized. Here, we combined tissue metabolite profiling with genome-guided screening and biochemical characterization of terpene synthases (TPSs). GC-MS analysis revealed variation in sesquiterpenoid profiles and dendrobine signals among tissues and developmental stages. Manual curation of the chromosome-level genome yielded 16 full-length TPS-a candidates. Functional screening in an FPP-supplying Escherichia coli system showed that three closely related genes on chromosome 1, DnTPS1~DnTPS3, produced copaborneol as their dominant product. The principal product of DnTPS1 was purified and identified by NMR spectroscopy, and a purified-enzyme assay confirmed its direct conversion of FPP to copaborneol. Fluorescence imaging in rice protoplasts and Nicotiana benthamiana leaves indicated predominantly cytosolic localization of DnTPS1. Guided by sequence comparisons and structural modeling, we tested 12 DnTPS1 variants and found that substitutions at W377 and I295 altered the relative distribution of sesquiterpene products. Phylogenetic and regional gene-order analyses placed DnTPS1~DnTPS3 in the same clade and identified related TPS candidates within corresponding genomic regions of six Dendrobium species. These findings establish that three D. nobile TPSs can form copaborneol and identify DnTPS1 residues that influence product selectivity, providing a basis for testing the proposed connection to dendrobine biosynthesis.

title: Distinct Progression Paths Underlie the Diversity of Pancreatic Papillary Cystic Neoplasms
abstract: Surgical decisions for intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs), precursors of pancreatic cancer, depend on distinguishing low-from high-grade dysplasia, a distinction that molecular markers could refine. We microdissected 433 tumor regions from 135 patients and integrated transcriptomics, deep-learning histology, and KRAS/GNAS RNA-called variants. RNA programs and morphological motifs separated lesions by phenotype, intestinal versus others, rather than by dysplasia grade.

title: Informatics Methods to Enhance Bacterial Peptide Detection
abstract: Detecting low-abundance bacterial peptides in samples dominated by human proteins using liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC MS/MS) is challenging. Bacterial peptides are typically far less abundant than host-derived peptides, and sequence similarity between bacterial and human peptides can complicate confident attribution to a bacterial origin. To address this problem, we developed and benchmarked an in silico spectral library protein identification workflow for detecting Staphylococcus aureus USA300 peptides against a background of A375 cells. Peptide and protein identifications obtained at a 1% peptide-level false discovery rate were compared between the in silico spectral library search and a conventional sequence database search across a defined bacterial dilution series containing 0, 1%, 2%, 10%, 25%, 50%, and 100% bacterial protein. A human sequence similarity filter was applied to identifications from both search strategies to reduce the likelihood of retaining human derived or human like peptide sequences. Both search strategies showed concentration dependent bacterial detection and shared a practical detection limit of approximately 1 to 2% bacterial protein but exhibited distinct performance profiles. The in silico spectral library search produced fewer bacterial-like background identifications in the human-only control, whereas MS2Rescore substantially increased spectral library identifications at higher bacterial concentrations, exceeding database search at 100% bacterial protein. The partially overlapping peptide sets identified by the two strategies indicate that they provide complementary coverage of the bacterial proteome.

title: Single-Cell Behavioromics Enables Fate Prediction of Individual Hematopoietic Stem Cells
abstract: Achieving near-single-cell precision in the prospective identification of long-term engrafting hematopoietic stem cells (LT-HSCs) remains challenging, likely because current static, point-in-time single-cell phenotyping technologies do not capture the dynamic nature of cell fate decisions. Here, we overcome this barrier by longitudinally tracking individual hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) in ex vivo niche cultures using live imaging, coupled with downstream immunophenotyping, single-cell transcriptomics, and transplant assays.

title: Chemically moulding intermetallics in two dimensions
Retention and biosynthesis of diverse nitroarenes in Escherichia coli after combinatorial nitroreductase gene deletions
Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning Approaches for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Diagnosis: Protocol for a Scoping Review
abstract: BackgroundAttention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) affects over 366 million adults and 139 million children worldwide, yet diagnosis remains fundamentally subjective, relying on clinical interviews, behavioral observations, and rating scales that yield inconsistent results across practitioners and settings. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) offer a paradigm shift toward objective, data-driven diagnosis by detecting complex patterns across neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and digital biomarkers that elude conventional assessment. Although AI-based ADHD research has grown exponentially, no comprehensive synthesis examines the full spectrum of data modalities, validation practices, and clinical translation readiness. This gap limits our understanding of which approaches are most promising for real-world implementation.ObjectiveThis scoping review will visually map the current evidence on AI-based ADHD classification with respect to predictive accuracy, data forms, data features, generalizability, and interpretability of models.MethodsThis scoping review will use the Joanna Briggs Institute approach to scoping reviews and follow the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines. Five electronic databases (IEEE Xplore, Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, and ACM Digital Library) will be systematically searched for peer-reviewed studies published between January 2019 and April 2026. Empirical studies in English involving the use of AI, ML, DL, or explainable AI to diagnose ADHD with a total sample size greater than 100 participants (ADHD and control groups combined) and a non-ADHD control group (individuals with typical development or healthy individuals) will be included. Two independent reviewers will screen the titles, abstracts, and full texts, and any conflicts will be resolved through either discussion or arbitration. A standardized Microsoft Excel template will be used to extract data that will include the following: bibliographic data, data modalities, data models, data validation approaches, performance metrics, and explainability approaches. Thematic and narrative analysis will be used to synthesize findings on 4 research questions that will address model performance, data modality contributions, data characteristics, and interpretability methods.ResultsThe scoping review began in December 2025. Analysis and screening are in progress, with the scoping review expected to be completed and submitted for publication in June 2026.ConclusionsThis scoping review will provide the first comprehensive synthesis of AI-, ML-, and DL-based ADHD diagnostic classification studies, mapping the evidence across data modalities, validation practices, interpretability methods, and clinical translation readiness. Findings will inform future methodological standards and support the translation of AI-based diagnostic tools into clinical practice.

title: Long-Range Conjugation-Sensitized Erbium(III) Shortwave-Infrared Emission in Porphyrin Molecular Wires
abstract: Shortwave infrared (SWIR; 1.0–2.0 μm) molecular emitters are increasingly attractive for bioimaging, optical sensing, and photonic technologies because photons in this spectral region experience reduced scattering and background interference. Yet the SWIR window is not optically uniform. Wavelength-dependent scattering and vibrational absorption create distinct optical subwindows, making spectral programmability essential for optimizing photon transport.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Enantioselective Scandium-Catalyzed Benzylic C−H Addition of Tertiary Anilines to Alkenes
abstract: Enantioselective C−H addition of aromatic amines to alkenes represents a highly efficient and direct approach for the synthesis of chiral alkylanilines. Herein, we report an enantioselective benzylic C(sp3)−H addition of tertiary anilines to alkenes, enabled by a bulky anilido-oxazoline ligand-supported scandium catalyst. This protocol delivers a broad range of chiral alkylated anilines in high yields (up to 96%) and enantioselectivities (up to 98:2 e.r.).

title: Pack and Extract: An Effective Graph-Based Approach for Feature Selection
abstract: Many molecular biology data sets contain thousands of features, such as genes in single-cell experiments or other omics data. Standard predictive models often perform poorly in such settings, as they tend to retain a large number of features and fail to adequately handle correlations among them. Combinatorial approaches, such as feature selection based on the Independent Dominating Set (IDS) model, have shown promising results, but appear to have been largely overlooked, possibly due to their high computational complexity. In this paper, we propose an improvement to IDS-based feature selection that (i) favors features exhibiting greater diversity and (ii) generalizes the notion of independent dominating set to a node packing model. The resulting formulation is used as an intermediate step within the feature selection process. We evaluate our approach on five genetic data sets and compare the results with those obtained using existing methods. Our experimental results demonstrate notable improvements in predictive accuracy over traditional models, as well as increased stability of the selected feature sets.

title: Research Evolution and Emerging Trends in Fruit and Vegetable Quality Assessment and Sorting: A Bibliometric Analysis of Analytical and Intelligent Sensing Technologies
abstract: Fruit and vegetable sorting is an important postharvest process for reducing losses and maintaining product quality. This study aimed to characterize the research landscape, knowledge evolution, and emerging technological trends in fruit and vegetable sorting from a bibliometric perspective. Publications from 2000 to 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and China National Knowledge Infrastructure databases. CiteSpace was used to analyze 1,387 publications through annual publication trends, collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence, clustering, and burst detection.

title: Cryptic Methylation Enables Amino-Maleimide Formation in Ligiamycin Biosynthesis
abstract: Maleimide is a rare but powerful pharmacophore in natural products, yet its biosynthetic logic remains poorly understood. Here, we elucidate the biosynthesis of ligiamycins, bacterial decalin–amino-maleimide metabolites from Streptomyces sp. NA07271. Genetic and biochemical studies revealed an unusual dispersed PKS–NRPS pathway, in which LigO1 hydroxylates a PCP-tethered precursor, followed by LigQ-mediated Dieckmann cyclization and LigN-catalyzed Diels–Alder cyclization to construct the tetramate-containing trans-decalin scaffold.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Targeted fine-tuning of machine-learning interatomic potentials for phonons and phase transitions
abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials are widely used as computationally efficient surrogates for density functional theory in atomistic simulations, enabling large-scale and long-time modeling of materials systems. Here, we investigate how different fine-tuning strategies affect the prediction of harmonic phonon band structures, thermal and elastic properties, and the potential-energy surface along unstable phonon modes. We show that substantial improvements can be achieved with very limited additional data, with as few as 10 material-specific training structures. We investigate targeted L 2 -SP ( L 2 -TSP) for this application, combining regularization toward the pre-trained model with selective fine-tuning of the first two representation-building layers, alongside transfer learning and multihead fine-tuning, with an additional comparison to low-rank LoRA for phonon prediction. Across 53 materials, L 2 -TSP achieves the most consistent overall performance, reducing phonon errors while also improving predictions of thermodynamic and elastic properties. Importantly, models with similar harmonic phonon accuracy can differ substantially in their prediction of dynamical instabilities and phase-transition behavior. Among the investigated approaches, L 2 -TSP shows the best overall agreement in dynamical-stability classification and in recovering the associated DFT reference phases, demonstrating improved generalization beyond the fine-tuning region. We implement L 2 -SP and L 2 -TSP in Equitrain , a model-agnostic software package for training and fine-tuning machine-learning interatomic potentials that can be applied beyond the MACE architecture considered here.

title: Controlling reactions via nucleophile sorting
abstract: Controlling the regio-, chemo-, and enantioselectivity of vicinal addition across olefins remains a challenging process. Now, a palladium-catalysed system has been developed, starting from propargylic alcohol precursors, that exploits tiered nucleophilicity between inner- and outer-sphere processes for precise control over the reaction outcome.

title: Disorder-induced nuclear-transition doublet at nominally cubic $^{229}$Th sites
abstract: The $^{229}$Th nuclear clock transition is inhomogeneously broadened even at sites of nominally cubic symmetry, where the electric-field gradient of the ideal lattice vanishes. We show that dilute static point-defect disorder produces a doublet with a zero at the quadrupole-free frequency. The doublet is symmetric in the isotropic approximation; size misfit point defects introduce a small lobe asymmetry without removing the zero. Charged and size-misfit defects share inverse-cube scaling and an approximately common normalized profile, whose width separates into a host-controlled background and a term linear in the $^{229}$Th density. In a heavily doped $^{229}$Th:CaF$_2$ crystal [Nature 657, 626 (2026)], the thorium-linked contribution is comparable to the measured 1.1 MHz width; in a lightly doped crystal [arXiv:2606.08870], the 0.9 MHz width bounds the host background. Neither spectrum shows the predicted dip, which points to the presence of extended defects in both crystals. If the predicted dip is resolved, it can provide a nuclear-clock discriminator referenced to the quadrupole-free nuclear transition frequency.

title: Integrative Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analyses Identify S100A8 as a Link Between Myeloid Inflammation and Mitophagy Dysregulation in Crohn’s Disease
abstract: Crohn's disease (CD) involves chronic mucosal inflammation and disrupted mitochondrial homeostasis, but genes linking myeloid inflammation to mitophagy remain incompletely defined. We integrated three training transcriptomic cohorts with two cross-cohort evaluation cohorts, protein-protein interaction analysis, machine learning, immune deconvolution, and single-cell RNA sequencing. Virtual knockout and preranked gene set enrichment analyses were used to examine S100A8-associated regulatory and mitochondrial programs.

title: Electronically Nonadiabatic Dynamics of O2 + O Collisions on Sixteen New Machine-Learned 3 A ″ Global Potential Energy Surfaces
abstract: High-energy O2 + O collisions on the 3A″ potential surface manifold of O3 provide a challenge for multistate nonadiabatic dynamics because covalent valence states and ionic configurations become strongly mixed in dynamically accessible regions. We developed a global machine-learned compatible potential-energy matrix (CPEM) for a 16-state nonadiabatic description of O2(X) + O(3P) dynamics with 3A″ symmetry, trained on XMS-CASPT2 data and augmented with physically motivated treatments of O2+ + O– ionic character where they are important.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Influence of the Pore Structure on the Activity and Stability of Non-precious Metal Catalysts for Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells
abstract: The activity/performance of non-precious metal catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in fuel cells is critically dependent on the pore structure of the catalyst layer, but a systematic understanding of how micropores and mesopores affect activity and stability remains limited. In this work, we employ a sacrificial template method to prepare a series of FeNC catalysts with variable weight fractions (from 0.125 to 0.75) of SiO2 template, followed by pyrolysis, SiO2 removal, and re-pyrolysis.

title: Silver doping induced fluorescence enhancement of gold nanoclusters combined with machine learning for detection of quercetin
abstract: A novel fluorescence sensing method of quercetin (Que) was constructed based on gold and silver bimetallic nanoclusters (L-Cys@Au-Ag NCs) that were prepared by sonochemical synthesis. In comparison with gold nanoclusters, the bimetallic nanoclusters produced enhanced fluorescence along with a blue-shift, which is achieved by Ag doping to engineer the aggregation states of the Au(I)-thiolate motifs in the NC shell. Since the fluorescence was quenched after the addition of Que, a rapid-response and highly selective method to detect Que has thereby been established using L-Cys@Au-Ag NCs.

title: Nuclear–Electronic Orbital Coupled Cluster Theory with the Nuclear Hartree Product Representation for Multiple Quantum Nuclei and Application to Geometric Isotope Effects
abstract: Nuclear–electronic orbital (NEO) methods treat specified nuclei, typically protons, quantum mechanically on the same level as electrons within quantum chemical calculations. This approach allows the computationally efficient inclusion of nuclear quantum effects such as nuclear delocalization, anharmonic zero-point energy, and tunneling into energy calculations, geometry optimizations, and dynamics. NEO coupled cluster (NEO-CC) methods recover correlation to an extent that enables prediction of accurate ground-state properties for moderately sized systems. Herein, NEO-CCSD(T), which includes all relevant single and double electron and nucleus excitations, as well as perturbative triple excitations, is formulated with the nuclear Hartree product representation for an arbitrary number of quantum nuclei. Compared to the nuclear Slater determinant representation, iterative convergence of the t-amplitude equations, as well as the preceding NEO Hartree–Fock procedure, is significantly faster for multiple quantum protons. Moreover, perturbative corrections in methods such as NEO second-order Møller–Plesset perturbation theory and NEO-CCSD(T) are more accurate using the nuclear Hartree product representation, most likely due to more physically reasonable virtual orbitals. Electronic frozen natural orbital truncation is implemented to extend the accessible system size while maintaining accuracy. These combined methods are used to calculate interaction energies of systems with multiple hydrogen bonds, as well as energies of water clusters with up to 24 quantum protons. In addition, NEO-CCSD(T) with the nuclear Hartree product representation is used to predict hydrogen/deuterium geometric isotope effects, incorporating the necessary anharmonic zero-point energy, for FHF–, a water dimer, and HF clusters of up to five molecules. These examples show that NEO-CCSD(T) with the nuclear Hartree product representation is an efficient and accurate method for incorporating nuclear quantum effects into ground-state calculations.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Spatial Proximity and Charge Transfer: Two Key Factors Governing Brønsted/Lewis Acid Synergy in Dealuminated H-ZSM-5 Zeolites
abstract: In dealuminated zeolites, extra-framework Al (EFAL) species released from the zeolite framework can act as Lewis acid sites (LAS) and exhibit a synergistic effect with neighboring Brønsted acid sites (BAS). However, the factors governing this synergy remain elusive. In this study, we elucidate how BAS and EFAL species cooperatively modulate the acidity of dealuminated H-ZSM-5 zeolites and then extend this understanding to the activation of propane.

title: Zn-Modified MoS2 Catalyst for Efficient CO2 Hydrogenation to CH3OH
abstract: Hydrogenation of carbon dioxide (CO2) to methanol (CH3OH) using hydrogen produced from renewable energy sources is a promising pathway for carbon recycling and energy storage. Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2), with its typical layered structure, holds significant industrial potential for low-temperature CO2 hydrogenation to CH3OH. The in-plane sulfur vacancies of MoS2 are considered active sites for their catalytic activity on hydrogenation of CO2 to CH3OH, while the edge sulfur vacancies lead to over-hydrogenation to produce methane (CH4).

title: Metal–Organic Cages as Porous Photosensitizers for Polyoxometalate Catalysts
abstract: Ionic metal–organic cages (MOCs) offer a unique platform to promote the reactivity of their functional counterions by forming “porous functional salts” (PFSs), but the role of MOCs has so far been limited to structuring and porogenic agent without strong coupling of properties. Herein, we report a new PFS, built from the assembly of the stable and noble-metal-free Keggin-type polyoxometalate (POM) SiW12O404– (SiW12) with a cationic Zr-based metal–organic cage (ZrT-NH2).

title: Influence of Exchange–Correlation Functional on Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials’ Accuracy: A Systematic Study of Borosilicate Glasses
abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have emerged as a strategy to accelerate molecular simulations, offering the promise of quantum chemical accuracy at a cost close to that of classical force fields. They are commonly trained on reference data obtained at the DFT level, which is itself a sufficiently affordable method to generate thousands of configurations and associated energies and atomic forces. However, this approach suffers from a major underlying challenge, which is rarely addressed: the choice of exchange–correlation functional.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Selective Nitrate-to-Nitrite Electroreduction on Ag/Au Core-Shell Nanocubes
abstract: Electrochemical nitrate reduction (NO3RR) offers a promising route for the production of valuable fertilizers and nitrites (common food preservatives), yet the relevant active sites remain poorly defined. Here, we combine density functional theory (DFT) with operando electrochemical scanning tunneling microscopy (n-EC-STM) to analyze tunneling current noise and establish structure–activity relationships in Ag/Au(111) and Ag/Au(100) model systems. DFT calculations show that Ag overlayers strengthen nitrate adsorption relative to bare Au and facilitate the initial NO3* → NO2* step. The adsorption energetics depend on both the structure of the surface facet and adsorption geometry, with tridentate nitrate adsorption generally favored on Au(100)-based surfaces and more variable behavior on Au(111)-based surfaces. Experimentally, Ag-coated Au(111) and Au(100) exhibit strong coverage-dependent NO3RR activity, with maximum activity near completion of an Ag monolayer on both facets. AgML/Au(100) consistently outperforms AgML/Au(111). n-EC-STM identifies Ag(100)-like monolayer terraces as the dominant active sites for NO3RR, whereas adjacent Au sites remain inactive. The same design principle is reproduced in Au{100} nanocubes, where Ag5nm@Au43nm/C with a thinner Ag shell outperforms Ag11nm@Au43nm/C and Au43nm/C. Together, these results identify terrace-confined Ag monolayers on Au as the key active sites for the electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction and highlight the roles of strain, ligand presence, and electronic effects at the Ag/Au–electrolyte interface.

title: Coupling of photoexcitation and grain-boundary disorder in the inverse Hall-Petch plasticity of nanocrystalline CdTe
abstract: The mechanical reliability of nanocrystalline semiconductors limits the durability of photovoltaic and optoelectronic devices, yet how grain size and electron-hole (e-h) excitation jointly govern their plasticity remains poorly understood at the atomic scale. Here we use molecular dynamics (MD) driven by machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) to investigate the shear deformation of nanocrystalline CdTe across effective grain diameters of 4.33 to 13.86 nm in the ground state and under two photoexcited electronic states.
